newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rate change seen signaling govt confidence.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rate change seen signaling govt confidence.

text.p: Brazilian policy-makers' decision to cut December interest rates to 1.74 percent indicates the government is not too concerned about the mounting trade gap or the pace of economic activity, analysts said.

"The decision shows that (they) are confident that the economy is not overheating and that the trade deficit is not a worry but is rather a natural consequence of economic opening," said Rio de Janeiro investment bank Fonte-Cindam in a report.
Brazil's Monetary Policy Committee (Copom) late Wednesday set the December rate at 1.74 percent, down from 1.78 percent in November.
